 5. 5465-0601-0003 6. Checking ### Checking #### Warnings and key information NOTICE The scavenge air receiver safety valve is calibrated at the factory and does not require any adjustment. 1. Checking the scavenge air receiver safety valve Check the scavenge air receiver safety valve by loosening the counter nut and turn the forced opening screw to open the valve approx. 10 mm. Use a piece of cloth to wipe out any dirt from the O-ring packing and close the valve again. Tighten the counter nut. If this operation cannot be performed smoothly, the safety valve must be dismantled and cleaned. ![](manual/58548175-ccef-4d6a-987c-f597b7d4d225/images/jpg/18014402360363915__Web.jpg) Copyright © 2024 MAN Energy Solutions * Home * Language * english * Home

query: What precautions should be taken when opening the crankcase or working with flammable materials on an engine to prevent fire and explosions?
pos: ﻿ Fire 1. 9836048 2. L9836048 3. Engine data 4. Description 5. D50002-02 6. Fire ### Fire If the crankcase is opened before the engine is cold, welding and the use of naked light will involve the risk of explosions and fire. The same applies to inspection of oil tanks and the space below the cooler. Attention should furthermore be paid to the danger of fire when using paint and solvents with a low flash point. Porous insulating material drenched with oil from leakages is easily inflammable and should be renewed. See also: "Ignition in Crankcase" in section 503/603. ﻿ Work during Repairs 1. 9836048 2. L9836048 3. Operation of Engine 4. Description 5. D50105-05 6. Work during Repairs ### Work during Repairs • **Crankshaft:** Carry out deflection measuring of the crankshaft, See "Checking of main bearings alignment (Autolog)", Working Card 510-01.00. • **Turbocharger:** If the recordings show that the charging air conditions have changed radically, cleaning of turbocharger or charge air cooler or other action should be effected, see separate instruction manual for turbocharger. • **Nuts and bolts:** Tighten all nuts and bolts in the crankcase, see "Data for torque moment", Description 500.40. Also retighten foundation bolts and check the chocks. • **Camshaft gear train:** Check the various gear wheels for the camshaft(s). • **Pneumatic valves:** Drain starting air pipes for condensed water. Check solenoid valve for overspeed stop and optionally, charge air by-pass valve and waste gate valve. • **Lub. oil cooler:** If the performance records indicate increased lub oil temperature or pressure drop, the oil cooler should be dismantled and cleaned.
